findings.title: updateEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
findings.body: In updateEvent selectedCalendar is computed as externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is falsy the else branch searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same falsy value, which never matches, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined instead of falling back to the booking's destination calendar. The Google events.update/patch calls then receive undefined calendarId and fail. Previously it fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
findings.body: In deleteEvent calendarId is computed as externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is null/undefined the fallback searches for externalId equal to null/undefined and always returns undefined, so deletion falls back to primary instead of the stored destination calendar. Previously it used event.destinationCalendar.externalId. This breaks deletes for bookings without an explicit externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty in Meet fallback
findings.body: In EventManager.create the code does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] then checks mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar" without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined or [] the destructured value is undefined and accessing .integration throws TypeError, aborting booking creation. Bookings without a destination calendar, which previously took the fallback path via optional chaining, now crash. It should be mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

findings.title: Collective team calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar, then collective hosts are added via evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). When it is null the optional chain no-ops and all teamDestinationCalendars are silently lost. Subsequent creation only writes evt.destinationCalendar[0] to the Booking, so secondary hosts never get calendar invites. Initialize to [] instead of null.

findings.title: Inverted slug condition in organization creation
findings.body: The spread was changed from ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) to ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}). The original set slug directly when team billing was disabled and only set requestedSlug when enabled. The new code does the opposite: sets slug when billing is enabled and sets no slug when disabled. This breaks org creation in both modes and is unrelated to the destinationCalendar fix.

findings.title: updateLocation loses externalCalendarId in references
findings.body: In updateLocation referencesToCreate is built as externalCalendarId: result.externalId. Results there come from CalendarManager.updateEvent, which never returns externalId or credentialId (unlike createEvent which does). So externalCalendarId is always undefined and newly created booking references lose the calendar ID needed for future updates/deletes. It should preserve booking.references externalCalendarId or the event destination.

findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar contract broken and tests inconsistent
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from single object/null to array, which changes the public webhook payload shape. The PR updates only the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation to [] while BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null. Consumers expecting an object or null will break, and the e2e suite will fail for the unchanged cases. This is a breaking API change needing migration/docs and consistent test updates.
